findings.summary: Committed returns can lose lifecycle event with no retry path
findings.details: submitReturn and cancelReturn persist the return, then rely on ReturnEventProducer to publish after commit. The producer calls kafkaTemplate.send() after the DB transaction commits, does not store an outbox record, does not wait on or attach failure handling to the send future, and only catches JSON serialization errors. If Kafka is unavailable or send fails asynchronously, the committed return has no durable event and no recovery mechanism. A retry is also not safe (duplicate check rejects already-created active return).
findings.tierReason: severity=high, confidence=0.90 (>=0.70), alreadyHandled=false — stage is in $SOFT_STAGES so outcome is advisory
findings.recommendation: Persist return events to outbox table in same transaction; retry from outbox with DLQ visibility. Handle send() future failure callback. This is F5 Foundation scope — fix in ReturnEventProducer shared infrastructure.

classificationRules.blockingThreshold: severity critical/high AND confidence >= 0.70 AND not alreadyHandled

adversarial-review.codexOutput: Verdict: needs-attention. No-ship: the return state commits before the Kafka side effect is durably recorded, so a successful API call can leave downstream return processing permanently unaware of the request.
